Search Bank of Japan metadata with bounded output

Source: R/metadata.R
search_boj_series.Rd

Searches the official BOJ metadata CSV for text in the selected name, category, notes and series-code fields. The cached file is scanned in chunks, so even the large Tankan catalogue is not materialised as one in-memory object. At most limit matching rows are retained. Use boj_metadata() when the complete bounded metadata table is required.

Usage

search_boj_series(
  query,
  db,
  language = "both",
  regex = FALSE,
  limit = 100L,
  cache_dir = boj_cache_dir(),
  refresh = FALSE,
  offline = FALSE,
  max_age = 24 * 60 * 60,
  timeout = 60,
  retries = 3L,
  wait = 1,
  max_bytes = 128 * 1024^2,
  include_groups = FALSE,
  deadline = NULL
)

Arguments

query

One non-empty character string. It is matched against the series code and the selected language's name, category and notes fields.

db

A BOJ database identifier, such as "FM08". It is converted to uppercase after validation; an identifier with a syntactically valid shape can still be rejected by the BOJ API if that database is not available.

language

Output language: "both", "en", or "jp". "both" retains paired Japanese and English text fields; "en" and "jp" retain only the requested language's name, unit, category and notes.

regex

Logical flag. If FALSE (the default), query is literal and fixed; if TRUE, it is a case-insensitive Perl-compatible regular expression. Invalid expressions raise readboj_parameter_error before downloading the metadata.

limit

Positive whole-number maximum matching rows retained and returned. The default is 100; it is a bound, not a request to materialise the full source catalogue.

cache_dir

Character path to the snapshot cache. The default is boj_cache_dir(), which uses the readboj.cache_dir option or tools::R_user_dir("readboj", "cache"). Missing cache subdirectories are created as needed.

refresh

Logical flag. When TRUE, bypasses a current cached request snapshot and obtains a fresh response. It is validated even when offline = TRUE.

offline

Logical flag. When TRUE, requires a valid cached snapshot and makes no network request. It is useful for deterministic replay.

max_age

Non-negative number of seconds for which a cached snapshot is considered current; Inf permits any age. The default is 24 hours.

timeout

Non-negative per-request timeout in seconds. The default for metadata requests is 60 seconds.

retries

Non-negative whole number of retries for transient transport or HTTP failures. The default is 3; non-transient failures are not retried.

wait

Non-negative number of seconds used between pages, code batches and retries. It is skipped for offline reads and is bounded by deadline.

max_bytes

Positive maximum decompressed response bytes per page. The default is 128 MiB; oversized responses fail with readboj_size_error before parsing or caching.

include_groups

Logical scalar. TRUE retains hierarchy heading rows without a series code; FALSE (the default) excludes them.

deadline

An optional absolute POSIXct/POSIXlt deadline shared by the metadata download, retries and delays. A bounded default is created when omitted.

Value

A base data.frame in source order, with at most limit rows, row names reset, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, and a readboj_provenance attribute. Its columns and types are the same as boj_metadata() after language filtering: db, series_code, the retained language name/unit/category/notes fields, frequency, integer layer1–layer5, character start_time/end_time, Date last_update, and logical is_series. Empty results retain the corresponding zero-row schema. Provenance additionally records query, result_limit, scan = "chunked", source/cache identity, transfer encoding, BOJ date/message ID, parser schema and package version.

Details

Literal searches are case-insensitive and use fixed matching. With regex = TRUE, query is interpreted as a Perl-compatible regular expression and matching remains case-insensitive. In language = "en" or "jp", only fields in that language plus series_code are searched; with language = "both", both language versions are searched. Group headings are excluded by default and can be included with include_groups = TRUE. Rows are retained in source order until limit is reached; no result rows are deduplicated.

The metadata response is fetched over HTTPS and cached using the same content-addressed snapshot, offline, retry, timeout, and absolute-deadline rules as boj_metadata(). CO remains subject to the same large-catalogue guard only when using boj_metadata(); this chunked search is the intended bounded discovery path.

Errors and side effects

Invalid arguments, invalid regular expressions, malformed or changed CSV schemas, row limits, API/transport failures and unavailable offline snapshots raise typed readboj_*_error conditions. The function may access the network and create cache files below cache_dir; it does not write search results to the working directory.

Examples

# The fixture shows the same bilingual schema without network access.
metadata_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "metadata-bilingual-utf8.csv", package = "readboj"
)
metadata <- read_boj_snapshot(
  metadata_path, type = "metadata_csv", db = "FM08", encoding = "UTF-8"
)
metadata[grepl("monthly", metadata$name_en, fixed = TRUE),
  c("series_code", "name_en", "is_series")]
#>   series_code                 name_en is_series
#> 2    SYNTHM01 Synthetic monthly index      TRUE
#> 3    SYNTHM02  Synthetic monthly rate      TRUE

if (identical(Sys.getenv("READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")) {
  search_boj_series(
    "exchange", db = "FM08", language = "en", limit = 10L,
    cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-live-example-cache"),
    timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 8 * 1024^2
  )
} else {
  message("Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run the live BOJ example.")
}
#> Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run the live BOJ example.
